q: A budget officer describes the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget of a workshop to a trainee. It is best described as:

options.A: A final Demand for Grants of the workshop
options.B: A part of the Stores Budget of the railway
options.C: A budget of the earnings expected from workshop outturn
options.D: An outlay (suspense) budget, the expenditure finding final allocation under Capital, Revenue or Stores heads on transfer of the outturn

e: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense budget is an outlay or suspense budget, as expenditure is finally allocated to Capital, Revenue or Stores heads only on transfer of outturn.

q: The cost accounts of a workshop do not float free of its Government accounts. The connecting link between the cost accounts and the financial accounts of a workshop is:

options.A: The Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books
options.B: The Stores Ledger kept in the depot
options.C: The Contractor's Ledger of the workshop
options.D: The Traffic Book of the railway

e: The link between cost and financial accounts is the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense head in the financial books and the Workshop General Register in the cost books, which must agree.

q: Workers are kept back on overtime in a shop, but the extra work is not for any one urgent job in particular. The overtime premium, i.e., the extra amount paid over the normal rate for such overtime hours, is ordinarily charged to:

options.A: The job on which the worker happened to be working last
options.B: Shop on-cost
options.C: The Capital account of the workshop
options.D: The Pension Fund

e: Overtime premium for hours not worked for any one urgent job in particular cannot be charged to a job, so the extra amount over normal rate is charged to shop on-cost.

q: For components manufactured regularly in a workshop, standard costs are prescribed and maintained. This is done so that:

options.A: Actual job costs need never be compiled for such components
options.B: No on-cost need be charged on such jobs
options.C: The components can be sold to the trade at the standard cost
options.D: The actual cost of each batch or job can be compared with the standard cost and the variations analysed for cost control

e: Standard costs for regularly manufactured components let actual batch or job cost be compared with the standard and variations analysed for cost control.

q: During a check of the Workshop General Register it is found that labour and material have been booked to a wrong work order. The correction of such a wrong booking is effected by:

options.A: Transfer entries debiting the correct work order and crediting the wrong one, passed under proper approval
options.B: Erasing the original entry in the shop records
options.C: Booking the amount again to the correct work order without any adjustment of the wrong booking
options.D: Writing off the amount to the Pension Fund

e: Wrong booking to a work order is corrected by transfer entries debiting the correct work order and crediting the wrong one, under proper approval, without erasing records.

q: In the annual accounts of a railway, the balance standing under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense does not appear as a liability or a receipt. It is reflected in the Balance Sheet of the railway as:

options.A: A liability of the railway
options.B: A revenue receipt of the year
options.C: An asset, representing the work-in-progress in the workshops
options.D: A part of the Pension Fund

e: In the railway Balance Sheet, the Workshop Manufacturing Suspense balance is shown as an asset representing work-in-progress in workshops, not as a liability or receipt.

q: A shop needs more covered space and an extension to its building is sanctioned. The cost of constructing such an extension to a workshop building is charged:

options.A: To Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.B: To shop on-cost of the shop housed in the building
options.C: To a revenue standing work order
options.D: To Capital/Depreciation Reserve Fund through a works estimate

e: Cost of an extension to a workshop building is charged to Capital or Depreciation Reserve Fund through a works estimate, not to suspense, on-cost or a revenue standing order.

q: A cost clerk is drawing up the list of charges that may legitimately enter the cost of a workshop job. Which of the following should be kept OUT of that list?

options.A: Direct material consumed on the job
options.B: Proforma on-cost, i.e., Provident Fund contribution and depreciation
options.C: Interest on the capital invested in the workshop
options.D: Shop on-cost and general on-cost

e: Interest on capital invested in the workshop is kept out of job cost in workshop costing. Direct material, on-cost and proforma on-cost are legitimate elements of cost.

q: In the terminology of cost accounting, the 'on-cost' of a workshop, which covers the indirect expenses of manufacture, corresponds broadly to:

options.A: Prime cost
options.B: Direct expenses chargeable to a job
options.C: Administrative overheads of the Railway Board
options.D: Factory (works) overheads

e: On-cost, covering indirect expenses of manufacture, corresponds broadly to factory or works overheads in cost accounting terminology.

q: An outside body approaches a workshop for execution of a work in the workshop. Work executed in a railway workshop for private parties or outside bodies is:

options.A: Never permitted under any circumstances
options.B: Undertaken only with the sanction of the competent authority, its full cost together with departmental charges being recovered from the party
options.C: Executed free of charge as a public service
options.D: Charged at the cost of material only

e: Work for private parties or outside bodies is undertaken only with sanction of the competent authority, and its full cost together with departmental charges is recovered from the party.

q: Moulding sand is consumed in the foundry on castings generally and cannot be traced to any single casting. Its cost in workshop costing is borne:

options.A: By the pattern shop as its own expense
options.B: By the stores depot as a stock loss
options.C: As part of the foundry's process/on-cost charges, spread over the castings produced
options.D: By debit to Capital

e: Moulding sand consumed generally on castings and not traceable to a single casting is borne as part of the foundry process or on-cost charges, spread over castings produced.

q: At the end of a shift, loose scrap is collected from a shop floor and it cannot be linked to any particular job done in the shop. Such scrap is accounted for by:

options.A: Crediting its value to the last job completed in the shop
options.B: Debiting its value to Workshop Manufacturing Suspense
options.C: Treating it as a personal perquisite of the shop incharge
options.D: Crediting its value to shop on-cost

e: Loose scrap collected from the shop floor that cannot be linked to any particular job is credited to shop on-cost, reducing the indirect charges of that shop.

q: A job taken up in a workshop is given up midway and is not to be completed. The expenditure accumulated on it under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense is:

options.A: Automatically transferred to the Pension Fund
options.B: Adjusted under the orders of the competent authority, and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under the suspense head
options.C: Recovered from the wages of the workers who worked on the job
options.D: Carried forward unchanged from year to year without any orders

e: Expenditure on a job abandoned midway is adjusted under orders of the competent authority and is not allowed to remain indefinitely under Workshop Manufacturing Suspense.

q: A finished article is ready to be taken out of the workshop premises to the stores depot. Material or finished articles are allowed to be taken out of a railway workshop premises only:

options.A: On the verbal permission of the chargeman
options.B: Against a personal surety of the worker carrying them
options.C: Under a gate pass issued by the competent authority
options.D: After the close of the financial year

e: Material or finished articles can be taken out of workshop premises only under a gate pass issued by the competent authority, as a control against unauthorised removal.

q: A new machine has to be erected in a shop and the existing machines of the workshop have to be kept in repair. The section of the workshop primarily responsible for such installation, maintenance and repair of the machinery and plant is the:

options.A: Pattern shop
options.B: Upholstery and trimming shop
options.C: Paint shop
options.D: Millwright shop

e: The millwright shop is primarily responsible for erection of new machines and for maintenance and repair of existing machinery and plant of the workshop.

q: A workshop engages fresh hands in place of workers who have left, and spends money on recruiting and training them. In cost accounting, such expenditure on recruiting and training is treated as:

options.A: A direct labour cost of jobs
options.B: Overhead (on-cost), as it cannot be charged to any particular job
options.C: A direct material cost of jobs
options.D: A capital expenditure

e: Expenditure on recruiting and training fresh hands cannot be charged to any particular job, so it is treated as overhead or on-cost in cost accounting.

q: At the gate of a workshop, the time office records the arrival and departure of the staff of every shop. The cost of running this time office is borne as:

options.A: General on-cost, since the time office serves the workshop as a whole
options.B: Shop on-cost of the erecting shop only
options.C: A direct charge on the first job taken up each day
options.D: Proforma on-cost of the workshop

e: The time office at the gate serves the workshop as a whole by recording attendance of all shops, so its cost is borne as general on-cost.

q: A clerk is posted to one shop only, where he keeps that shop's records and is not booked to any individual job. His wages are treated in workshop costing as:

options.A: Direct labour of the jobs done in that shop
options.B: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.C: Indirect labour charged to the shop on-cost of that shop
options.D: General on-cost of the workshop

e: A clerk posted to one shop only, keeping its records and not booked to individual jobs, is indirect labour and his wages are charged to shop on-cost of that shop.

q: While compiling the full cost of a manufactured article, a notional element is added so that the cost can be compared with trade rates. Which of the following charges forms part of this proforma on-cost?

options.A: Pension contribution in respect of workshop staff, charged notionally
options.B: Power consumed by the machines of a shop
options.C: Wages of the foreman of a shop
options.D: Consumable stores used in a shop

e: Pension contribution for workshop staff is a notional proforma on-cost charge, added to make workshop cost comparable with trade rates, and is part of proforma on-cost.

q: Work orders in a workshop are first classified by the head of account to which the job is chargeable. Apart from this classification, they are also broadly distinguished according to the nature of the work as:

options.A: Audited and unaudited work orders
options.B: Cash and credit work orders
options.C: Local and foreign work orders only
options.D: Manufacture work orders and repair work orders

e: Apart from classification by head of account, work orders are broadly distinguished by nature of work as manufacture work orders and repair work orders.

q:
Consider the following statements about the leave salary of shop staff in a workshop:
1. Leave salary for a period of sanctioned leave is booked to the last job on which the worker was engaged before proceeding on leave.
2. Leave salary cannot be charged to any job and is therefore borne as an overhead charge of the workshop.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Leave salary cannot be charged to any job, as the worker was on no job during leave, so it is borne as an overhead charge of the workshop. Statement 2 alone is correct.

q: A workshop accounts clerk is classifying the charges that enter the cost of outturn only notionally, so that the workshop's cost can be compared with trade prices. In this classification, the pension contribution in respect of workshop staff belongs to:

options.A: Shop on-cost
options.B: General on-cost
options.C: Proforma on-cost
options.D: Direct labour booked on jobs

e: Pension contribution for workshop staff is a notional charge entering cost only for comparison with trade prices, and is therefore classified as proforma on-cost.

q: A proposal is made to load interest on the capital invested in a workshop into the cost of its jobs, so as to make job costs fully comparable with the prices of outside suppliers. The correct position in workshop costing is that:

options.A: Interest on capital is loaded on capital jobs only, and not on revenue jobs
options.B: Interest on capital is loaded at a rate fixed by the Workshop Accounts Officer
options.C: Interest on capital forms part of proforma on-cost
options.D: Interest on capital is not charged as an element of the cost of a workshop job

e: Interest on capital is not charged as an element of cost of a workshop job, even to make costs comparable with outside suppliers, and is not part of proforma on-cost.

q: The standards room of a workshop maintains the master gauges and calibrates the working gauges and measuring instruments used in all its shops. The cost of maintaining this room is borne in workshop costing as:

options.A: General on-cost, since the room serves the workshop as a whole
options.B: A direct charge on the job under inspection at the time
options.C: Proforma on-cost of the workshop
options.D: A charge on the stores depot attached to the workshop

e: The standards room maintains master gauges and calibrates instruments for all shops, serving the workshop as a whole, so its cost is borne as general on-cost.

q: In the maintenance records of workshop machinery, the indicator 'MTTR' shows, for the machines of a shop:

options.A: The average interval between two successive breakdowns of a machine
options.B: The average time taken to repair a machine after a breakdown and restore it to working order
options.C: The total time for which all machines of the shop remained idle in a year
options.D: The time for which a spare machine is kept in reserve for the shop

e: MTTR, Mean Time To Repair, shows the average time taken to repair a machine after breakdown and restore it to working order, a maintenance performance indicator.

q:
Consider the following statements about articles which deviate slightly from the prescribed specification:
1. Such an article may be accepted under a concession (deviation permit) if it is assessed to be fit for its intended use.
2. Acceptance of such an article requires no approval of a competent authority and no record need be kept of the concession.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: An article deviating slightly from specification may be accepted under a concession or deviation permit if fit for intended use, with competent approval and record. Statement 1 alone is correct.

q: During the Periodic Overhaul of a coach, a component is found still within its wear limits, but the component figures in the list of items prescribed for renewal at every overhaul. The correct course is to:

options.A: Retain the component, since it is still serviceable, and cancel the renewal
options.B: Postpone the renewal of the component to the next overhaul of the coach
options.C: Renew the component only if a spare happens to be available in the shop at the time
options.D: Renew the component in accordance with the prescribed list, its present serviceability notwithstanding

e: A component in the prescribed list for renewal at every Periodic Overhaul must be renewed as per that list, even if still within wear limits and serviceable at that overhaul.

q: A bill is being prepared for the Periodic Overhaul of rolling stock belonging to another railway, so that the full cost of the work is recovered from the owning railway. Besides the labour and material booked on the job, the bill must also cover:

options.A: Only the direct expenses incurred on the job
options.B: A share of the cost of overhauling the home railway's own stock
options.C: The on-cost and proforma charges applicable to the job
options.D: The departmental charges of the home railway's headquarters office alone

e: A bill for Periodic Overhaul of another railway's stock must recover, besides labour and material, the on-cost and proforma charges applicable to the job, to cover full cost.

q:
Consider the following statements about surplus material returned by a shop to the stores depot:
1. The work order is credited as soon as the shop reports that the material has become surplus, whether or not the depot has received it.
2. The credit is given on the depot acknowledging receipt of the material under a return note, so that the credit is supported by the depot's accountal of the material received back.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Credit for surplus material is given only when the depot acknowledges receipt under a return note, supporting the credit by depot accountal. Statement 2 alone is correct.

q: The accounts office is about to transfer the outturn of a finished job when it notices that the cost booked on the job has overrun the amount sanctioned in its estimate. What must be done first?

options.A: The overrun must be regularised through a revised or supplementary estimate sanctioned by the competent authority
options.B: The outturn should be transferred at once and the overrun ignored
options.C: The amount of the overrun should be charged to the shop on-cost of the shop
options.D: The amount of the overrun should be recovered from the workers engaged on the job

e: If job cost overruns the sanctioned estimate, the overrun must first be regularised by a revised or supplementary estimate sanctioned by the competent authority before transfer.

q:
Consider the following statements about semi-variable overheads of a workshop:
1. Semi-variable overheads are partly fixed and partly variable in behaviour, changing with the volume of outturn but not in direct proportion to it.
2. The fixed element of a semi-variable overhead item disappears as soon as the outturn of the shop falls to nil.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Semi-variable overheads are partly fixed and partly variable, changing with outturn but not in direct proportion. The fixed element does not vanish at nil outturn, so statement 1 alone is correct.

q: A workshop starts an additional shift in a shop, and the whole pay of an extra chargeman engaged solely for the supervision of that shift is added to the shop's supervision cost at once, instead of the cost rising gradually with the outturn. In terms of cost behaviour, this supervision cost is an example of:

options.A: A variable cost
options.B: A step cost
options.C: A sunk cost
options.D: A direct cost chargeable to jobs

e: Pay of an extra chargeman for an added shift rises in one lump when the shift starts, not gradually with outturn, which is the behaviour of a step cost.

q:
Consider the following statements about the distribution of workshop overheads:
1. In the primary distribution, overheads are apportioned to all cost centres of the workshop, production and service centres alike.
2. In the secondary distribution, the costs collected at the service centres are reapportioned to the production shops served by them.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: In primary distribution overheads go to all cost centres, production and service alike, and in secondary distribution service centre costs are reapportioned to production shops. Both are correct.

q:
Consider the following statements about two service centres of a workshop:
1. The power house of a workshop supplies power to the machine repair shop, and the repair shop maintains the plant of the power house, so that each of these service centres renders service to the other.
2. In the secondary distribution of overheads, the cost of such mutually serving service centres is reapportioned taking their services to each other into account, and not by ignoring the mutual service.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Power house and machine repair shop serve each other, and in secondary distribution their costs are reapportioned taking mutual services into account. Both statements are correct.

q: A workshop worker is deputed for a part of a month on work which is not covered by any measured job or allowed time. For that part of the month, under the incentive arrangements, he is:

options.A: Paid bonus at the highest rate earned in the shop during the month
options.B: Paid no wages at all for that part of the month
options.C: Paid his time-rate (fall-back) wages for the period, without incentive bonus for that period
options.D: Treated as absent without leave for that period

e: For work not covered by any measured job or allowed time, the worker gets his time-rate or fall-back wages for that period, without incentive bonus for that period.

q: A senior clerk in the workshop office and a supervisor engaged on general duties, neither of them attached to any shop or group covered by the incentive scheme, claim incentive bonus for a month. Their claim stands as under:

options.A: Bonus is payable to them at the average rate of the whole workshop
options.B: They are outside the incentive scheme and no incentive bonus is payable to them
options.C: Bonus is payable to them at double the rate of direct workers
options.D: Bonus is payable to them only out of the savings in material cost

e: Staff not attached to any shop or group covered by the incentive scheme, like general office and supervisory staff, are outside the scheme and get no incentive bonus.

q: A fitter works in the machine shop for the first half of a month and is then posted to the erecting shop, where he works for the rest of the month. For costing and incentive purposes, his month is dealt with by:

options.A: Booking his whole month's time and bonus in the machine shop, from which he was transferred
options.B: Denying him incentive for that month altogether
options.C: Charging his wages for the whole month to general on-cost
options.D: Booking his time, and computing his incentive, separately for the period worked in each shop, according to the work done and the scheme applicable there

e: When a worker moves between shops mid-month, his time is booked and incentive computed separately for the period in each shop, per the work done and scheme applicable there.

q:
Consider the following statements about Mid-Life Rehabilitation (MLR) of coaches:
1. Work relating to Mid-Life Rehabilitation of coaches is executed in workshops under work orders through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, like other workshop work.
2. Mid-Life Rehabilitation work is executed without any work order and its cost is charged directly to shop on-cost.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Mid-Life Rehabilitation of coaches is executed in workshops under work orders through Workshop Manufacturing Suspense like other workshop work. Statement 1 alone is correct.

q: In a carriage workshop, all the material needed for a coach's overhaul is assembled in advance as one complete set, ready for issue to the overhaul job when the coach is taken in hand. This advance assembly of the material is known as:

options.A: Batching of outturn
options.B: Kitting of POH material
options.C: Pooling of stores
options.D: Loading of machines

e: Advance assembly of all material needed for a coach overhaul as one complete set, ready for issue when the coach is taken in hand, is called kitting of POH material.

q: A trainee in the workshop accounts office asks under which Plan Head the Manufacturing Suspense of workshops figures in the railway's classification of heads. It is:

options.A: Plan Head 73 - Miscellaneous Advances
options.B: Plan Head 71 - Stores Suspense
options.C: Plan Head 32 - Track Renewals
options.D: Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense

e: Manufacturing Suspense of workshops figures under Plan Head 72 in the railway classification of heads, distinct from Plan Head 71 for Stores Suspense.

q: For a proposal to construct a new workshop building and expand a production unit, provision in the railway's Works Programme is sought under:

options.A: Plan Head 21 - Rolling Stock
options.B: Plan Head 42 - Workshops and Production Units
options.C: Plan Head 41 - Machinery and Plant
options.D: Plan Head 72 - Manufacturing Suspense

e: Provision for a new workshop building and expansion of a production unit is sought under Plan Head 42, Workshops and Production Units, in the Works Programme.

q: A shop needs small consumable items every day, and indenting the depot afresh for every small need would hold up work. Such items are therefore generally held:

options.A: In the personal custody of the chargeman, without any accountal
options.B: In the cash office of the workshop
options.C: Only in the main stores depot, shops not being allowed to hold any stores at all
options.D: In the shop itself under an imprest arrangement, replenished from the stores depot as the stores are consumed

e: Small consumable items needed daily are held in the shop under an imprest arrangement and replenished from the stores depot as consumed, avoiding fresh indents for every need.

q: Unlike a job work order, which is cleared when its outturn is transferred to the final head, an on-cost standing work order of a shop, on which the shop's indirect expenses are collected, is cleared by:

options.A: Transferring its balance out as outturn to Stores
options.B: Treating it as a job executed for another railway
options.C: Distribution of the amount collected on it over the jobs done in the shop
options.D: Keeping it open for ten years and then writing it off

e: An on-cost standing work order is cleared by distributing the indirect expenses collected on it over the jobs done in the shop, not by transferring outturn to Stores.

q:
Consider the following statements about the power house of a workshop:
1. The cost of the power house, which serves all the shops, is first collected as a service cost centre.
2. That cost is thereafter brought into the cost of jobs by direct charging to each individual job, without reference to the shops served.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: The power house cost is first collected as a service cost centre and then apportioned to shops served, not charged directly to individual jobs. Statement 1 alone is correct.

q: Opening the folio of a work order in the Workshop General Register, one can see, besides the labour, material and on-cost debited to it:

options.A: The leave account of the workers engaged on the job
options.B: The price ledger balance of every stores item used on the job
options.C: The programme of the workshop for the following year
options.D: The credits given to the work order on transfer of its outturn and the balance still outstanding against it

e: A work order folio in the Workshop General Register shows, besides labour, material and on-cost debited, the credits on transfer of outturn and the balance still outstanding.

q: An inspector examines an article midway through its manufacture, rather than waiting for its completion. The object of this stage inspection is to:

options.A: Replace the final inspection of the finished article altogether
options.B: Detect defects at an intermediate stage itself, so that further work is not wasted on an article already defective
options.C: Fix the wages of the workers engaged on the article
options.D: Price the material issued for the article

e: Stage inspection at an intermediate stage detects defects early, so further work and cost are not wasted on an article already defective, without replacing final inspection.

q: Production of a batch of components is about to begin on a freshly set machine. The first piece off the machine is examined thoroughly before the batch proceeds, chiefly to:

options.A: Close the batch work order after the first piece itself
options.B: Fix the piece rate payable to the operator
options.C: Verify the machine setting, tools and method, so that the whole batch is not produced defectively on a wrong setting
options.D: Credit the cost of the batch to the stores depot

e: First-piece inspection after a fresh machine setting verifies setting, tools and method before batch production proceeds, so the whole batch is not produced defectively.

q: To judge how fully a repair workshop has used its overhaul capacity in a period, the comparison made is between:

options.A: The units actually overhauled and turned out during the period and the overhaul capacity available in the workshop for that period
options.B: The wages paid in the period and the wages paid in the previous period
options.C: The material consumed in the period and the stock held in the depot
options.D: The number of work orders opened and the number of shops in the workshop

e: Use of overhaul capacity is judged by comparing units actually overhauled and turned out in a period with the overhaul capacity available in the workshop for that period.

q: Midway through the year, a workshop revises its Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates at the periodical budget review. The revision is based mainly on:

options.A: The cash balance available in the workshop imprest
options.B: The figures of the previous year repeated without change
options.C: The number of staff retiring during the remaining period
options.D: The trend of actual outlay and outturn during the year and the revised programme of manufacture and overhaul work for the remaining period

e: Revision of Workshop Manufacturing Suspense estimates at the budget review is based mainly on trend of actual outlay and outturn and the revised programme for the remaining period.

q: Articles turned out on a job fail the final inspection as not conforming to specification. Till they are put right and accepted, or otherwise disposed of under competent orders, their cost:

options.A: Is transferred to the stores depot as good stock at full cost
options.B: Is written off by selling the articles as scrap without any record
options.C: Is charged to general on-cost without any orders
options.D: Remains under the job in Workshop Manufacturing Suspense, the articles not being transferred out as outturn

e: Articles failing final inspection are not transferred out as outturn, and their cost remains under the job in Workshop Manufacturing Suspense till they are rectified, accepted or otherwise disposed of.
